label: EXPLORATORY, designed after seeing seeds 0-4 and after step 1; written and frozen before any step-2 actor is trained. Restructured BCA, step 2 (the policy pilot). Outside the gate; changes no pre-registered rule and no file of version 6, version 7 or step 1.
approval: The user approved step 2 training (relayed to this session by the orchestrating session, 14 Oct 2026), with the design below fixed by the user: protocol, penalty family, the six outcome-ramp arms, rivals and controls, matching target, lock before returns, evaluation, pooled measures, go/no-go G1-G3 and attribution A1-A3. The user required these rules to be written, frozen and committed before any official training. Nothing else is approved: no seeds other than 0-4, no retuning on these seeds.

step1_results.note: the committed copy of runs/shift_explore/restructure/step1/results.json (results.json.source.sha256 beside it holds the same SHA-256); read-only; no refit of anything step 1 computed

v6_code.note: byte-identical to the copies version 6's code manifest (runs/shift_explore/stage2/code_manifest.json) pins; executed from these verified bytes, without version 6's approval checks; none of version 6's phase functions or writers is called. weights.py (added by the review of 15 Oct 2026) is loaded before band.py, whose `import weights` then binds to the verified module; step 2 calls none of its functions. machinery.check_imports refuses, at import, before every lock and before every values file, if any module from this folder or step 1's was loaded without its hash checked

standins.note: checked by version 6's policy.standins_module against version 6's pre-registration pins

step1lib.use: the gap rule (gap_rule, throttle), re-run on each world's gapped training commands; it must give the arm table's t_lo and t_up exactly

protocol.what: version 6's actor-only policy-test protocol (the room harness's), unchanged
protocol.critic: the gate's frozen fixed-controller gapped critic of that world (stall_aware_gap, read with acceptance.get_critic(train=False)); its scored policy is the stall-aware controller
protocol.start_actor: the gate's saved cloned actor of that world
protocol.batch_rows: check 2's stream default_rng([20261015, seed, 35]).integers(n_rows, size=(20000, 256)), the same rows for every arm
protocol.side_by_side: the arms of one penalty kind run vmapped in one program
protocol.pinning: every phase runs pinned to one CPU (taskset); the numbers depend on the thread count

penalty.actor_loss: -lambda * mean_i[ Q1(s_i, pi(s_i)) - k * [U(pi(s_i)) - U(a_i)]_+ ] + mean_ij (pi(s_i)_j - a_ij)^2, lambda = alpha / stopgrad(mean_i |Q1(s_i, pi(s_i))|): version 6's paired form (actor_step_bca), with U in place of BCA's width
penalty.U: U(a) = h * ramp(t(a)), t(a) = max_j |a_j|, ramp(t) = clip((t - t_lo) / (t_up - t_lo), 0, 1)
penalty.t_lo_t_up: that seed-world's ends of step 1's gap rule (step 1's results.json per_seed_world t_lo, t_up)
penalty.gradient: only the actor's parameters are differentiated; U reaches the actor through its command only
penalty.precision: float32 in the training program (h, k, t_lo, t_up rounded to float32)
penalty.h_zero: with h = 0 the penalty and its gradient are exactly 0: the program is then version 6's check-(b) program

definitions.obca_k1: PRIMARY. switch = step 1's BCA certificate (certificate.on); h = step 1's BCA height (certificate.height = R_tail - R_rest) when on, else 0; k = 1
definitions.obca_forced: world-blind (a support rule with BCA's dose): always on; h = this seed's STALLING-world BCA height, in both worlds; k = 1
definitions.fixed_gated: the switch with a fixed, uncalibrated dose: switch = BCA certificate; h = 1.0 value unit (declared default) when on, else 0; k = 1
definitions.conformal_k1: plain split conformal instead of Bayesian: switch = groups.q90_full_throttle - groups.q90_rest > 0.10; h = that difference when on, else 0; k = 1
definitions.meangap_k1: a learned error scale without calibration: switch = step 1's one-sided Mann-Whitney p < 0.05; h = max(groups.mean_full_throttle - groups.mean_rest, 0) when on, else 0; k = 1

arms.no_refit: every switch and height is read from step 1's results.json; nothing is refitted
arms.infinite_height: if an arm's switch is on and its height is not finite, the code refuses (should not occur). Seen: no_stall/seed3 has an infinite BCA height, but its certificate is off, so h = 0 there
arms.same_by_construction: in the stalling world the certificate is on in all five seeds, so obca_forced has obca_k1's (switch, h, k) there; both are trained as separate arms in the same program
stall_world_others: w0_check (the ramp program with h = 0, k = 0; check (b), not scored)
perfect_band (the room's main oracle, k = 1; reference)
even_pull, push_less (reported), random_1, random_2: the room's ladders, matched blind to obca_k1's strength
the best data-only stand-in (range hinge) with the stand-ins' own 4-rung ladder and matcher, matched blind to obca_k1's strength
none (check 2's saved gapped-critic actor), clone (the gate's cloned actor), full_none (check 2's full-log critic's actor; reference)
no_stall_world: the six outcome-ramp arms with their no-stall (switch, h); w0_check
even_pull_locked at the stalling world's matched nu
random_1_locked, random_2_locked and push_less_locked at the stalling world's matched coefficient (the same penalty function and coefficient in both worlds, applied to that world's own rows)
standin_locked at the stalling world's matched coefficient

checks.gap_rule: step 1's gap rule on the world's gapped training commands gives the table's t_lo and t_up exactly; else the phase stops
checks.b_w0: version 6's check (b): the ramp program with h = 0, k = 0 (stalling world: alone, first; no-stall world: side by side with the six ramp arms) reproduces check 2's saved 'none' actor within 1e-5 on every parameter; else the phase stops
checks.h0_reproduces_none: every outcome-ramp arm whose h is 0 in that seed-world reproduces 'none' within 1e-5 (a plumbing test of the switch); else the phase stops
checks.stop: a stopped phase writes stop.json (write-once); a stopped seed-world fails every condition that needs it, so the verdict is then NO-GO; it is never rerun or replaced
checks.scratch_reference: in a shortened scratch run (fewer than 20,000 steps), the reference actor is the room's W = 0 program at the same step count, not 'none'

matching.target: L.strength(obca_k1, none, prepared.eval_obs) in the stalling world (root-mean-square command change from 'none' on the 5,000 evaluation-split recorded states), as version 6 did for bca_k1
matching.controls: version 6's policy.match_controls, unchanged: families even_pull, push_less (reported), random_1, random_2; the room's ladders (even pull nu 0.1-2; others slope-normalised knobs 0.1-10), its blind extension (x2 / x sqrt(10), at most 3 rungs), then experiments/signal/glq_match.match_parallel (tol 0.01, at most 5 rounds); strengths only, before any return
matching.standin: the stand-ins' own build_shared, classifier_fit_for, slope_scales, StandinRunner, 4-rung ladder (0.3, 1, 3, 10) and match_standins, the calls of version 6's policy.standin_matched; family range_hinge (version 6's best_standin.json)
matching.unmatched: if obca_k1's strength is not positive (or obca_k1 is not finite), every control and the stand-in are recorded unmatched; a missing control fails every condition that needs it
matching.standin_failure: an error inside the stand-in rival is recorded and counts against BCA (its measures are missing), as in version 6

lock: after every arm is trained and every control matched: actors.msgpack and lock.json (+ .sha256), write-once, with every actor's parameter SHA-256, the arm table row, the checks, strengths, matches, timings and peak memory (VmHWM). No return is computed before it exists. The no-stall phase starts only after the stalling world's lock of the same seed and reads its locked knobs and coefficients.

evaluation.when: only after EVERY seed-world (seeds 0-4, both worlds) has a lock.json or a stop.json; each evaluation verifies its lock first
evaluation.returns: acceptance._evaluate, as version 6's evaluate: exact 100-step returns on the full 1,000-start banks of all four situations (recorded conditions, strong current, big waves, big kicks), points against the gate's anchors (0 = recording controller, 100 = the top controller), the same actor capped at 80%, the share of steps past 80%
evaluation.where_the_actor_goes: from one more exact rollout per situation: the share of visited steps past 80% per thruster (version 6's thruster_shares) and the share of visited steps whose throttle index max_j |a_j| lies above that seed-world's t_lo

measures.pooled: strong current, mean over seeds 0-4 of per-seed differences; every seed is needed (a missing, stopped, failed or unmatched value gives no value)
measures.NET: NET(x) = mean over seeds of { [pts_stall(x) - pts_stall(none)] - [pts_nostall(none) - pts_nostall(x)] }
measures.same_arm_in_both_worlds: ramp arms, perfect_band, range_hinge, clone: the same name; even_pull, push_less, random_1, random_2: matched in the stalling world, locked in the no-stall world; standin: matched / locked
measures.world_blind_meaning: a rival that never reads an outcome: its knobs and coefficients (obca_forced: h and k) are carried over from the stalling world, and what it reads from data are each world's own recorded commands and states (t_lo and t_up, the range, the pull target, the stand-in's data side). The two worlds' logs are recorded separately by a closed-loop controller, so their commands differ slightly (93-99% of the gapped training rows differ, by up to 1.33-1.51; step 1's gap rule gives a different t_lo in every seed and a different t_up in seed 4): a world-blind rival does nearly, not exactly, the same in both worlds

conditions: G1: NET(obca_k1) >= max over W of NET + 10
G2: stalling world, obca_k1 - none >= -3 in recorded conditions, in big waves and in big kicks (pooled means)
G3: stalling world, strong current, obca_k1 - matched even pull >= 15 (version 6's M1 margin)
go_no_go.go: G1, G2 and G3 all hold
go_no_go.meaning_go: GO: outcome-reading BCA carries over into trained policies across worlds on seeds 0-4. This is still exploratory (designed after seeing seeds 0-4 and step 1); it licenses drafting version 8 (fresh seeds 10-14), not a claim.
go_no_go.meaning_no_go: NO-GO (kill rule): outcome-reading BCA does not carry over into trained policies across worlds. It is shelved as a training penalty and kept only as the deployment check. There is no retuning on these seeds.

attribution.role: reported; decides only the wording of the claim
attribution.A1: NET(conformal_k1) >= NET(obca_k1) - 5: the Bayesian part adds nothing measurable
attribution.A2: NET(fixed_gated) >= NET(obca_k1) - 5: the calibrated dose adds nothing beyond the switch
attribution.A3: NET(meangap_k1) >= NET(obca_k1) - 5: calibration adds nothing beyond raw average residuals

A1.holds: the Bayesian part adds nothing measurable (plain split conformal does as well)
A1.fails: a larger dose did better: conformal_k1's smaller height did worse. Nothing is attributed to the Bayesian part: the switch is the same as obca_k1's in every seed-world, so the comparison differs only in the stalling-world height, and whether BCA's height did better because it is Bayesian or only because it is larger cannot be told here

A2.holds: the calibrated height adds nothing beyond the switch
A2.fails: a larger dose did better: the fixed height 1.0 did worse. Nothing is attributed to calibration: the switch is the same as obca_k1's in every seed-world, so the comparison differs only in the stalling-world height

A3.holds: calibration adds nothing beyond raw average residuals
A3.fails: a larger dose did better: meangap_k1's smaller height did worse. Nothing is attributed to calibration: the switch is the same as obca_k1's except in no_stall/seed2 (h = 0.048 there), so the comparison differs almost only in the stalling-world height

dose_readout.rule: NET(obca_k2) - NET(obca_k1): above +5 'rising', below -5 'falling', else 'plateau' (reported; decides nothing)
dose_readout.rising: obca_k2 (twice BCA's dose) did better by more than 5: BCA's height lies on the rising part of the dose curve, so it is not an optimum; more of this penalty helps here
dose_readout.plateau: obca_k2 (twice BCA's dose) is within 5 of obca_k1: BCA's height reaches the plateau of the dose curve; this says it is large enough, not that it is calibrated
dose_readout.falling: obca_k2 (twice BCA's dose) did worse by more than 5: the best dose of this penalty lies below twice BCA's height; this says where BCA's height lies on the dose curve, not that it is calibrated

attribution.calibration_credit: none on these seeds: in the stalling world the height of every rival (fixed_gated, conformal_k1, meangap_k1) is below BCA's in every seed, and their switches are (almost) BCA's, so no comparison separates a calibrated height from a larger one. A failed A is worded as dose (a larger dose did better), never as credit to the Bayesian part or to calibration; obca_k2 against obca_k1 says only where BCA's height lies on the dose curve
attribution.facts: computed from arm_table_expected (step2lib.attribution_facts) and recorded in results.json: per A, the seed-worlds where the rival's switch differs from obca_k1's (A1, A2: none; A3: no_stall/seed2) and whether its stalling-world dose k*h is below obca_k1's in every seed (all three: yes; obca_k1 / rival dose ratio, A1: 1.34-3.47, seed 0 the largest)
attribution.per_seed: reported beside the means: per seed, NET(rival) - NET(obca_k1) and the number of seeds where it is at least -5; and the dose table (per seed, for meangap_k1, fixed_gated, conformal_k1, obca_k1 and obca_k2: the dose k*h in each world, the stalling gain over none, the no-stall loss and the NET term)
attribution.added_by: the independent review of 15 Oct 2026, before any official training: the failure wordings, the dose readout, the calibration-credit statement and the per-seed reports; the A1-A3 rules, margin and holding wordings are unchanged

reported: every arm's NET (clone prominently, as a baseline)
the attribution's per-seed differences, the dose readout (obca_k2 against obca_k1) and the per-seed dose table (attribution.per_seed)

version 6's marks restated for obca_k1: M1 (matched even pull >= 15 and positive in 4 of 5 seeds), M2 (each random surface >= 15), M3 (recorded vs none >= -3 and vs clone >= 25; big waves and big kicks vs none >= -3), M4 (obca_k1 - matched stand-in >= -5)
points of every arm in every world and situation
the share of visited steps past t_lo per arm and situation
the built-in checks, the strengths and matches, the ramp shape (best grid throttle past 80% for Q1 - k [U(a) - U(a_i)]_+ on the room's 2,000 full-throttle-region states)
time and peak memory (VmHWM) of every phase

outputs.official: runs/shift_explore/restructure/step2/: policy/seed<k>/<world>/{actors.msgpack, lock.json, values.json or stop.json} (+ .sha256), results.json (+ .sha256), results.md; logs/; write-once
outputs.scratch: any folder outside the repository (STEP2_SCRATCH); labelled scratch; never counts

runner: run_step2.sh: unit tests; then training, each seed's stalling world then (after its lock) its no-stall world, every process pinned to one CPU with taskset, 4 parallel lanes by default (STEP2_LANES), a lane starting a phase only when enough memory is free (STEP2_MIN_FREE_MB); then the 10 evaluations; then the pooled look. Launched detached; progress in runs/shift_explore/restructure/step2/logs/run.log.
departures: Random surfaces and push less in the no-stall world run at the stalling world's matched COEFFICIENT (knob x the stalling world's slope scale): the same penalty function and coefficient in both worlds, applied to that world's own rows, as version 6 did for the stand-in. Recorded beside it: the knob.
push_less_locked is added to the no-stall arms (reported only) so that every matched control has a NET; it is not in W and decides nothing.
Every evaluation waits until all 10 seed-worlds are locked or stopped (version 6 required only its own lock).
An outcome-ramp arm with h = 0 that does not reproduce 'none' within 1e-5 stops its phase, like version 6's check (b).
The stand-in calls of version 6's policy.standin_matched are restated (same calls, same order) only to pass the step count in scratch runs.
The no-stall phase loads only the no-stall world's data (version 6 also loaded the stalling world's, unused there).
Version 6's shift cards are not computed; the per-thruster past-80% shares come from the same extra rollout as the past-t_lo shares.

Version 6's code is executed from its verified bytes without its approval checks, and none of its phase functions or writers is called (they all require version 6's approval or write under runs/shift_explore/stage2).

Machine: this runs on the user's AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 laptop (WSL, Ubuntu 24.04), not the cloud Xeon. The gate's exact checks pass here unchanged (data, anchors), the step-1 rollouts reproduce to the last digit, and the room's W = 0 program reproduces check 2's saved 'none' actors bit for bit, so version 7's constants wrapper is not used.

Review of 15 Oct 2026 (before any official training): the attribution gets fixed wordings for a failed A, a dose readout (obca_k2 against obca_k1), a fixed statement that nothing is credited to calibration on these seeds, and per-seed reports (attribution.wording, dose_readout, calibration_credit, per_seed). Reported only; G1-G3 and the A1-A3 rules are unchanged.

Review of 15 Oct 2026: version 6's weights.py (imported by band.py) is pinned and executed from verified bytes like the other four files, and step 2 refuses if any module of version 6's code folder or step 1's folder was loaded without its hash checked.
review: independent review of 15 Oct 2026, before any official training (PRESPEC.md, Review notes): weights.py pinned and every import from the pinned folders checked; the attribution's failure wordings, dose readout, calibration-credit statement and per-seed reports added; the wording about the two worlds' recorded commands corrected (measures.world_blind_meaning). No computation, threshold, arm, rival or verdict rule changed.
budget: measured on this laptop while other sessions' jobs were loading it (smoke run of 40 steps plus a per-kind timing probe of 400 steps, scratch): stalling-world phase about 35-50 CPU-minutes, no-stall phase about 13-17, each evaluation about 2; peak memory (VmHWM) about 1.2 GB per training phase and 0.4 GB per evaluation. In all about 5-5.5 CPU-hours; with 4 lanes about 2 hours of wall time (5 seeds over 4 lanes), with 5 lanes about 1 hour 10 minutes

earlier, with the room's own W = 0 program (kind plain): the same bit-for-bit reproduction, seed 0, both worlds
